title: fix(spec): bound the form-row `scale` at the renderer ceiling of 100 (#19088)
body:
Fixes #19088

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

`FormFieldBaseSchema.scale` in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` — the per-field override a form row carries — was declared as any non-negative integer with no upper bound. It is the third declaration of `scale` to reach the platform ceiling #18972 bounded on the two in `data/field.zod.ts`: every consumer turns `scale` into decimal places, and both `Number.prototype.toFixed` and `Intl.NumberFormat`'s `maximumFractionDigits` throw a `RangeError` at 101, so a conforming declaration could not render. The row now carries that bound, and the refusal names both primitives, the `RangeError` and the legal maximum rather than saying "too large".

Evidence below is measured on this branch at `df3185cf9f`, base `origin/main` = `e6a03e649`, node v22.22.2.

## The card's premise, re-verified — one half of it is now false

The dispatch's hardest fence rests on PR #19083 being **open** and holding both `field.zod.ts` sites plus the module-private `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE`. Measured: **#19083 merged at 2026-09-18T17:48:04Z** as `021755abc4`, two days before the dispatch was written, and both bounds plus the constant are on `main` today.

The defect half of the premise is intact and was re-measured, not inherited: at the branch base `scale: 101` **parsed clean** on this row (bright control below). So the card stands; only the reason the fence gave for itself has expired.

**The fence was obeyed anyway.** `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` is untouched in this diff — the file surface the claim declares is `view.zod.ts` and its tests, and widening it is not a call this seat makes even when the in-flight PR that motivated the fence has landed. The consequence is stated plainly in the arm measurement below: route 3 could not be completed on both ends this round, and what remains is recorded rather than smuggled in.

## The shared-constant half — three arms, measured

| arm | what it costs | verdict |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| ① duplicate the literal in `view.zod.ts` | one platform fact recorded in a second place with nothing holding the two equal; a later consolidation still has to mint the shared home | viable, not taken |
| ② promote `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE` to a published export | `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts:132` re-exports `field.zod` with `export *`, so the constant lands on the `@objectstack/spec/data` surface: `Clause-②: yes`, at least `minor`, an at-tier contract review — **and it edits `field.zod.ts`**, which the fence forbids | refused, on both counts |
| ③ spec-internal, non-exported shared module | one new leaf file; **no cycle possible** (it imports nothing); **no published export** | **taken** |

Arm ③'s two open questions, both answered by measurement rather than by reading:

- **Can `view.zod.ts` import it without a cycle?** `packages/spec/src/shared/scale-ceiling.ts` has zero imports, so it is a graph leaf and cannot participate in one. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` exits 0 and `view.zod.ts` already imports eight other `../shared/*` modules.
- **Does it move the published surface?** No. `check:api-surface`, `check:api-surface-declarations`, `check:export-origins` and `check:declaration-map` are all green with the file added — `shared/index.ts` is an explicit list of `export *` lines, not a wildcard, and this module is deliberately absent from it. The precedent is established: `strict-object.ts`, `editability-boundary.ts`, `union-branch-policy.ts` and `section-group-reference.ts` all live there unexported, and `SELECT_OPTION_EDITABILITY_GUIDANCE` has zero occurrences in `packages/spec/api-surface/`.

**What arm ③ does NOT buy this round, stated rather than glossed.** Sharing has two ends, and the fence holds one of them: `field.zod.ts` keeps its own module-private `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE` and `SCALE_UPPER_BOUND_MESSAGE`, so the tree still records the number twice. The difference from arm ① is what the second copy is *for*: the new module is a home `field.zod.ts` can move into as a pure delete-and-import, buying no export and no review — and until it does, the two are held equal from this end by a pin that asserts the refusal text at both sites is **byte-identical**. A drift between the copies is a red test, not two divergent explanations of one platform limit.

## Acceptance — three legs

**Bright control (before the change).** At the branch base `e6a03e649`, against the built `packages/spec/dist/ui/index.mjs`:

```
scale:100    : PASS
scale:101    : PASS
scale:-1     : REFUSED code=too_small message="Too small: expected number to be >=0"
scale:2.5    : REFUSED code=invalid_type message="Invalid input: expected int, received number"
precision:101: PASS
```

`scale: 101` passed, so this round demonstrably narrowed something and the probe was never dead.

**Subject (after).** Same probe, same built artifact, rebuilt at `df3185cf9f`:

```
scale:100    : PASS
scale:101    : REFUSED code=too_big message="Decimal places cannot exceed 100 — the limit is the
               renderers', not a policy: every consumer turns `scale` into fraction digits, and both
               `Number.prototype.toFixed` and `Intl.NumberFormat`'s `maximumFractionDigits` throw a
               RangeError above 100, so a larger declaration is unrenderable rather than merely large.
               Declare at most 100 (an IEEE-754 double carries ~17 significant digits, so a meaningful
               display precision is far below it)."
```

`100` parses and round-trips; `101` is refused with a `too_big` issue at `[scale]` whose message names `toFixed`, `maximumFractionDigits`, `RangeError` and the legal maximum — the same text the two `field.zod.ts` sites produce, asserted as such rather than as prose.

**Dark control.** `scale: -1` and `scale: 2.5` are refused before and after with the **same code and the same message bytes** (`too_small` / "Too small: expected number to be >=0"; `invalid_type` / "Invalid input: expected int, received number"). The #8321 / #12174 refusals are untouched; only the top of the range moved. The test asserts those two messages by equality, not by regex, so a restatement of the bottom of the range turns it red.

**The platform fact re-measures every run, per the card.** `100` is never trusted as a literal: the pin probes `(1.5).toFixed(100 | 101)` and `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 100 | 101 })` for `RangeError` on every run and then asserts the schema's own accept/refuse boundary sits on the same number. If a future runtime moves either limit, the pin goes red and the declaration is re-argued. This is #18972's shape, copied.

## The `check-widening-tells` warning the dispatch raised — measured, and it did NOT block

The dispatch flagged #19099: `check-widening-tells` T1 can refuse the criterion-honest `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, making over-declaring the only unblocked path. Run against this branch's real diff:

```
node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff /tmp/pr.diff   ->  exit 0
✓ check-widening-tells: 4 changed file(s) — 2 judged against a declared surface (no widening tell), 2 NOT MEASURED.
```

So this diff is a **negative sample** for #19099, not another positive one. The two files judged against a declared surface are `view.zod.ts` and the new `shared/scale-ceiling.ts`; neither fired a tell. Worth recording for that card: T1 did **not** misfire on a `scale:` line that the diff re-emits in full to attach `.max(…)`, and T3 did not fire on a new file carrying two `export const`s that reach no entry point. The declaration stayed `no (narrowing)` on its merits; nothing was flipped to get unblocked.

## What this PR deliberately does not touch

- **`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** — the dispatch's fence, kept (see above). It is read-only input to one test assertion.
- **`precision`** — untouched on this row, as on the object-field row. It is a TOTAL digit count and reaches neither primitive, so the renderer-ceiling argument does not carry to it; a pin records that the omission was measured rather than missed. Whether the three `precision` arms should agree is its own judgement.
- **No renderer, no clamp, no fallback.** Refusing an unrenderable declaration at the door is this card; what a renderer should do when handed a large value stays objectui#9808's.
- **objectui is not changed** — the consumer chain is cited from the schema's own existing comment, not re-measured across repositories this round.

## Verification

| command | result |
| :-- | :-- |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` | exit 0 — 500 files, 14650 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/ui/view.test.ts` | exit 0 — 466 tests passed; the 7 new cases named individually under `--reporter=verbose` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` | exit 0 (base and head) |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | exit 0 after `--fix` regenerated `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx` (`gen:docs`) — the two `scale` descriptions, nothing else |
| `pnpm lint` (whole repo, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) | exit 0 at `df3185cf9f` |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | exit 0 — 9028 text files, no raw control bytes |
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` | exit 0 — 1 declared-breaking changeset, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff …` | exit 0 |
| gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` | 106 derived, all 106 run, each exit code captured before any pipe; `--ran` reconciles to 0 UNRUN |

**NOT MEASURED — seven of the derived commands, none of them a finding.** Each refuses its own prerequisite because it reads built `dist/` of packages this diff does not touch: `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture`, `check:docs-transcript-drift`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt` exit 3 with a PREREQUISITE NOT MET verdict; `check:skill-examples` refuses the same way but exits **1** (`packages/client-react/dist` holds no `.d.ts`), so `dispatch-gates --ran` classifies only six. Building that closure locally exceeded this container's foreground limit (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/client-react...' build`, killed at 570s). They are recorded as NOT MEASURED, not as green; CI builds the closure and runs them for real.

**Base.** This branch is not merged with `main` — it branched at `e6a03e649` and `main` has since moved. The intervening commits touch no `packages/spec/src` file (only the generated `packages/spec/liveness/*` ledger), so nothing above was measured against a file this branch also moves; the merge queue's rebuilt generation is the race-free joint check.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset` does not hold and no such label is written: `@objectstack/spec` publishes `dist` in its `files[]` and `src/**/*.zod.ts` besides, and this diff changes what the published artifact accepts at runtime. The changeset is a `minor` carrying the **BREAKING** banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, per the launch-window convention in which `major` is refused and breaking-ness rides the banner rather than the level. Its zero-hit reading: 126 `scale: N` declarations across `*.ts` / `*.tsx` / `*.json` / `*.mdx` / `*.yml` / `*.yaml` on this tree as the lit control, of which four read above 100 and all four are refusal fixtures or prose about them — zero authored declarations above the ceiling. Radius: this repository's tracked files; the known target outside it is a `sys_metadata` row already stored in a running deployment, which no in-repo instrument reaches (#18972 recorded the same blind spot).

## Acceptance notes

- **noted, not filed: the platform fact is still recorded three times in this tree.** `shared/scale-ceiling.ts` (new), `data/field.zod.ts`'s module-private copy, and `packages/objectql`'s `MAX_FORMULA_SCALE`. The first two are now pinned byte-equal from this side and the third cannot be folded in at all — `objectql` depends on `spec`, not the reverse, so the duplication there is structural. Successor for the first pair: whichever seat next holds `data/field.zod.ts`, where the adoption is a two-line delete-and-import against the module this PR lands and needs no export and no review. Successor for `MAX_FORMULA_SCALE`: none today.
- **noted, not filed: `precision` is bounded on one arm and unbounded on two others.** `CurrencyConfigSchema.precision` is `.max(10)`; `FieldSchema.precision` and `FormFieldBaseSchema.precision` have no maximum (`precision: 101` is measured to parse clean on this row, before and after). No renderer-ceiling argument applies to any of them, so this is not the same defect wearing another name, and whether the three should agree is a judgement about three different field arms rather than a bug. #18972 carried the identical note. Successor: none named — it is one line away from both sites, so whoever takes a `precision` decision takes all three.
- **noted, not filed: the dispatch's fence outlived its stated reason.** PR #19083 had already merged when the fence was written against it still being open. Recorded because the next card cut from the same seam will inherit the same sentence; the fence was still obeyed here. Successor: the PM loop that issues the next `field.zod.ts` card.
